statement: Everything below was published by Reactome or the Human Protein Atlas. Genesis did not measure, model or compute any of it, and nothing here may be presented as a Genesis experimental result.

catalystActivity: G protein-coupled receptor activity of GLP1:GLP1R:Heterotrimeric G(s):GDP [plasma membrane]
records.summationVerbatim: GLP-1R that has bound GLP-1 activates the alpha subunit of the heterotrimeric G-protein G(s) by protein-protein interaction between intracellular loop 3 of GLP-1R and G(s). The activation causes exchange of GDP for GTP by the alpha subunit of G(s).

literatureReferences.title: Functional Characterization of N-Terminally GFP-Tagged GLP-1 Receptor

sourceFacts.label: SOURCE_FACT
sourceFacts.claim: In human, GLP-1R with GLP-1 bound activates the alpha subunit of the heterotrimeric G protein G(s), causing GDP/GTP exchange.
sourceFacts.source: Reactome R-HSA-381706 (R-HSA-381706.4), "GLP1R:GLP1 activates G(s)", Homo sapiens, review status "five stars" (externally reviewed)
sourceFacts.verbatim: GLP-1R that has bound GLP-1 activates the alpha subunit of the heterotrimeric G-protein G(s) by protein-protein interaction between intracellular loop 3 of GLP-1R and G(s). The activation causes exchange of GDP for GTP by the alpha subunit of G(s).

citations.title: Functional Characterization of N-Terminally GFP-Tagged GLP-1 Receptor

notInFetchedSources.label: NOT_IN_FETCHED_SOURCES
notInFetchedSources.whatThisMeans: The two Reactome records fetched cover GLP-1R binding GLP-1 and the activation of G(s). Neither of them states the cAMP step. So the "-> cAMP" half of the requested chain is NOT source-backed by what this repository holds, and it is not written down here as if it were. Closing it needs the downstream Reactome reaction fetched and hash-recorded like these two.
notInFetchedSources.doNotInfer: That G(s) canonically raises cAMP is textbook knowledge. Textbook knowledge recalled by a model is not a source, and this file does not carry it as one.

inferences.label: INFERENCE_BY_GENESIS
inferences.statement: A functional cAMP-arm agonism assay is a reasonable readout for GLP-1R activation, which is the endpoint role D-151/D-152 already classify on.
restsOn: the SOURCE_FACT above, for the receptor-to-G(s) step
doesNotRestOn: any fetched source for the G(s)-to-cAMP step, which is missing
inferences.isNotEvidence: This is Genesis joining records. It is reasoning, not a published finding, and it is not evidence that any molecule activates anything.

rna.unit: nTPM for tissues, nCPM for single-cell types, as HPA reports them

sourceFacts.label: SOURCE_FACT
sourceFacts.claim: HPA reports GLP1R RNA as "Tissue enhanced" and "Detected in some", with tissue-specific values {"heart muscle":"2.6","pancreas":"8.6"} nTPM.

sourceFacts.label: SOURCE_FACT
sourceFacts.claim: At single-cell level HPA reports "Cell type enhanced", highest in Tuft cells 46.1, Pancreatic islet cells 23.3, Lacrimal acinar cells 19.0 nCPM.

sourceFacts.label: SOURCE_FACT_THAT_CUTS_THE_OTHER_WAY
sourceFacts.claim: HPA's OWN antibody staining does not support tissue expression: protein tissue specificity "Not detected", distribution "Not detected", immunohistochemistry reliability null, antibody ["CAB080541"].
sourceFacts.whyItIsHere: HPA's headline "Evidence at protein level" comes from UniProt and neXtProt ("Evidence at protein level"); HPA's own evidence level for this gene is "Evidence at transcript level". Quoting the RNA numbers without this line would overstate what HPA actually shows.

inferences.label: INFERENCE_BY_GENESIS
inferences.statement: Pancreas is the tissue with the highest reported GLP1R transcript level among those HPA calls specific, and pancreatic islet cells the highest among pancreatic cell types.
restsOn: the two RNA SOURCE_FACTs above, read as reported
inferences.isNotEvidence: A transcript level is not a protein level, a protein level is not a functional receptor, and none of this is a measurement Genesis made.

notInFetchedSources.label: NOT_IN_FETCHED_SOURCES
notInFetchedSources.whatThisMeans: Not fetched, so not reported. The HPA record is the only expression source this repository holds.

whatThisDoesNotLicense: A pathway record is not evidence that any molecule activates the receptor.
An expression record is not evidence that a molecule reaches that tissue or does anything there.
Binding is not functional agonism; docking is not agonism; a heterologous-system response is not a native-tissue response.
None of this changes any frozen gate, any sealed artefact, or D-144, D-151, D-152, D-153 or D-154.
